title: Timer-Driven Countdown View Model

docs.title: Managing model data in your app

hints: Ticks only count while running; the model decides what a tick means.
`tick()` guards `isRunning` and stops (and flags `finished`) at zero.
jsBridge: A timer-driven countdown in a view model: ticks come in from `Timer.publish` or `TimelineView`. React uses `setInterval` inside `useEffect` with cleanup, and SwiftUI's `.onReceive` ties the subscription to the view.

compass.q: React `useEffect(() => { const id = setInterval(...); return () => clearInterval(id) })`. What's SwiftUI's cleanup story?
The app goes to the background for 30 s. Does a `Timer` keep ticking? How do you stay accurate (store an end date)?
Counting ticks vs computing `endDate - now` each tick: which drifts?
`TimelineView(.periodic(from:by:))` vs `Timer.publish`: which is better for a countdown label?
